transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. On a Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer, damp clothes after two hours is most often caused by restricted airflow or laundry that was too wet to begin with. Before looking at internal parts like the heater element, we need to rule out these simple issues. 1. Clean the filters: Remove the lint filter from the door opening and rinse it under a tap. Let them drip dry before refitting.
2. Check your washing machine's spin speed: If clothes come out of the washer dripping wet, the dryer has to work much harder and may not finish in time. Ensure you are using a high spin cycle (e.g.3. Verify the load size: Overloading the drum restricts airflow. The drum should be no more than two-thirds full. If these are already clean and your wash routine is good, please let me know if the dryer feels hot to the touch during operation (carefully check the air outlet) or if it runs cool.

Did the filters: they had fluff and a waxy film, and water barely went through until I scrubbed them. Washer spin is 1200 and the loads are normal size. The drum is hot after 20 min, so it is heating. What next?

Good work on the filters; that waxy film is common with fabric softener and most likely restricts airflow. Since the drum is getting hot, we know the heating element is working, which rules out a heater failure. On condenser dryers like your Bosch WTN85201GB, the lint filter only catches the big bits of fluff. The air then passes through a heat exchanger (the condenser unit) where moisture is removed. If this gets blocked with fine dust and fluff, hot air can't circulate properly to dry the clothes, even if the drum feels hot. Please locate the condenser unit (usually behind a flap at the bottom front of the dryer). Let it drip-dry completely before putting it back in. Once you've done that, run a normal drying cycle again. If the clothes are still damp after cleaning the condenser, we'll look at the moisture sensors next.

Never cleaned the condenser before. Front of it was matted with lint, but it came clean with the shower head. Also vacuumed fluff out of the slot behind it. Ran a test cycle and clothes dried in about 100 minutes, container nearly full again.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That is excellent news. 1. Clean the lint filter after every cycle.
2. Remove and rinse the condenser unit at least once a month, or more often if you notice drying times increasing again. Let it drip-dry completely before putting it back in.
3. Avoid using too much fabric softener, as this contributes to the waxy film that builds up on filters. Your dryer is now functioning normally. If damp clothes return despite these cleanings being maintained, let me know.
